title: Longitudinal two-photon calcium imaging with ultra-large cranial window for head-fixed mice
protocol: Anesthetize the adult mouse in a chamber filled with 3% isoflurane in oxygen.
Clamp the nose of the mouse on the stereotaxic instrument.
Provide isoflurane (1%–1.5% in oxygen) from the nose clamp during surgery.
Maintain body temperature using a servo-controlled heating pad.
Inject baytril (10 mg/kg) and dexamethasone (2 mg/kg) subcutaneously to prevent infection and inflammation.
Disinfect the head skin with 70% ethanol and betadine.
Cover eyes with Vaseline to keep them from drying.
Cut out and remove the skin above the skull with scissors.
Expose the dorsal skull above the olfactory bulb, cerebral cortex, and cerebellum.
Clean the skull surface using a Kimwipe soaked with 70% ethanol.
Detach muscles on the lateral edges of the cerebellum to increase skull surface area.
Leave detached muscles posterior to the skull.
Detach lateral muscles near the auditory cortex to increase skull surface area.
Leave detached muscles at their original place.
Scrape off connective tissue from the skull surface using a scalpel.
Clean the skull surface using a Kimwipe soaked with 70% ethanol.
Use a needle fixed on a motorized micromanipulator to measure the height at each coordinate.
Equalize the heights between the bregma and the lambda.
Equalize the heights between ±2 mm lateral from the bregma.
Mark the following coordinates on the skull using a water-resistant permanent marker.
Find each coordinate using the needle.
Mark the coordinate using the marker.
Confirm the coordinate by sticking the needle down to the ink.
Remove extra ink by a drill.
Cover the dorsal skull with saline and wait for at least 30 seconds to make the skull semi-transparent.
Take a photo of the semi-transparent skull with the marked coordinates and the vasculatures on the cortex.
Thin the skull by drilling if necessary to achieve sufficient transparency for visualizing the cortical vasculatures.
Wash the glass plug with saline.
Place the glass plug on the skull to check the necessary craniotomy size for the window implantation.
Take off the glass plug and thin the skull along the edges of the intended cranial window using a drill.
Thin the skull along the edges of the cranial window and suture lines until the underlying vasculature pattern becomes clearly visible.
Remove bones in ascending order from #1 to #4 using forceps, sliding them toward the arrow direction.
Place a saline-soaked gelatin sponge on the bleeding site to stop bleeding.
Use a compressed air duster to clear skull debris during thinning.
Thin the skull along the midline and coronal suture lines without exposing the brain.
Cover the dorsal skull with saline and wait for at least 1 minute.
Remove the left parietal bone carefully from its edge using fine forceps.
Detach the left parietal bone except along the midline sinus, sliding it to the side.
Place gelatin sponges on any bleeding sites during removal of the bone.
Remove the right parietal bone carefully from its edge using fine forceps.
Detach the right parietal bone except along the midline sinus, sliding it to the side.
Place gelatin sponges on any bleeding sites during removal of the bone.
Carefully remove the left frontal bone from its edge using fine forceps.
Slide the fine forceps between the bone and dura if detachment is difficult.
Detach the left frontal bone except along the midline sinus, sliding it to the side.
Place gelatin sponges on any bleeding sites during removal of the bone.
Carefully remove the right frontal bone from its edge using fine forceps.
Slide the fine forceps between the bone and dura if detachment is difficult.
Detach the right frontal bone except along the midline sinus, sliding it to the side.
Place gelatin sponges on any bleeding sites during removal of the bone.
Clean the glass plug with saline and a Kimwipe.
Place the clean glass plug on the exposed cortex.
Push the glass plug down using the micromanipulator.
Attach a sharpened wooden bar to the manipulator for pushing the plug.
Apply gentle pressure to the brain through the glass plug, critical for stable imaging from medial cortical areas.
Adjust the pressure based on blood flow in the midline sinus, ensuring it is not too strong as to block blood flow or so weak that it allows dilation of the sinus.
Remove excess saline between the base glass and skull using Kimwipe.
Fill the gap between the base glass and skull with 3M Vetbond using a syringe.
Wait at least 30 seconds after applying 3M Vetbond before proceeding.
Remove any extra 3M Vetbond from around the window using Kimwipe.
Apply Krazy glue (cyanoacrylate glue) around the edges of the cranial window using a syringe with a 25G needle.
Ensure that the glass plug is stably glued to the skull before lifting the wooden bar.
Use a syringe with a 25G needle to apply Krazy glue to fixate the head bar and cranial window.
Mix dental acrylic cement with a double-ended carver.
Apply a thin layer of Krazy glue over the exposed muscles behind the cerebellum.
Mount dental acrylic cement until it reaches the height equal to the skull above the cerebellum.
Place the head bar behind the glass window.
Ensure the head bar is parallel to the skull before applying Krazy glue to secure its position.
Cover all exposed skull surfaces with Krazy glue, including lateral areas exposed in previous steps.
Apply dental cement using a double-ended carver.
Mix Krazy glue around the glass window on the skull surface.
Apply dental cement over the Krazy glue layer to build up the wall height.
Cover the head bar with Krazy glue followed by dental cement for stability.
Clean the glass window with a cotton swab soaked in 70% ethanol.
Inject buprenorphine subcutaneously at 0.1 mg/kg.
Take a photo of the cranial window after the cement dries.
Transfer the mouse to an animal cage and place it on a heating pad until recovery from anesthesia occurs.
If water-restriction is necessary, wait for at least 5 days post-surgery before initiating water restriction.
Perform two-photon calcium imaging from the target cortical areas.
Find the cortical vasculature patterns within the target field-of-views (FOVs).
Check the vasculature patterns on the photo from step 15 (Coordinate photo).
Identify corresponding vasculature patterns on the photo from step 37 (Post-surgery photo).
Head-fix the mouse under the two-photon microscope.
Adjust angles of both the animal stage and the objective lens to achieve uniform light reflection on the glass window.
Measure the rotational angle of the microscope (objective lens) using an angle gauge for reproducibility.
Measure the horizontal angle of the animal stage for reproducibility.
Perform two-photon imaging with a water-immersion objective lens.
Find the vasculature patterns of the target FOVs by referencing previous photos.
Adjust the angles of the animal stage and objective lens to make the glass window perpendicular to the light path through the objective lens.
Image the glass window while moving the z-depth up and down around the window.
Correct the angular discrepancy between the glass window and the objective lens based on the reflection line's movement direction during z-depth adjustments.
After correcting, ensure excitation light is uniformly reflected on the glass window.
Move the objective lens down to the target depth for imaging.
Start calcium imaging using software like ScanImage for data acquisition.
Record the angles of the animal stage and objective lens after imaging.
Remove motion artifacts and distortions from saved images using image registration algorithms such as PatchWarp.
Create a reference image by averaging all frames from a registered image in a reference session.
Set the angles of the animal stage to the recorded angles from step 46.
Set the angles of the objective lens to the recorded angles from step 46.
Find the target field of view based on cortical vasculature patterns.
Move the focus down to the same depth as before.
Compare the current field of view with the reference image's field of view.
Adjust the imaging depth and animal stage angle accordingly.
Start calcium imaging.
Begin the behavior task.
